measurement: repeated accessibility invoke on support-preview-button, with repaint between attempts
result: Five invokes - four in a row and one after closing and reopening the panel so the subtree was rebuilt - all returned without an exception, and the in-process trace produced ZERO lines every time. Repainting or rebuilding the subtree does not change the outcome, so this is not a one-frame or stale-snapshot effect.
wiring_comparison: Both elements are divs with .id, .accessibility_id, .role(Role::Button), .aria_label, .aria_keyshortcuts, .track_focus, .cursor_pointer and both .on_action(Activate) and .on_click. Differences: the toggle's label is state-dependent and its shortcut list includes Ctrl+D, while the preview button additionally carries .aria_description and a static label, and sits deeper in the child chain. Which of those differences, if any, decides dispatch is NOT determined.
mechanism_note: In the pinned gpui (395def7a), .on_click registers an AccessibleAction::Click listener during paint against the element's global id, and the listener is only registered inside the a11y-active branch. Both elements produce InvokePattern in the automation tree, so the action is advertised for both; what differs is whether the dispatch reaches the handler.
not_attempted: No product change: the next step would be a bisect of the structural differences (for example making the preview button identical to the toggle one property at a time), which is a product edit and needs a decision before it is made.
